blocks.title: Page 1
blocks.text:
GLEUHR WELLNESS PVT LTD
Skin & Hormones — PCOS, Thyroid, Imbalance
For counsellors · link the condition to her skin with empathy · doctor leads the medical detail
Why this conversation matters
Many clients carry PCOS, hormonal imbalance, or thyroid issues — and these directly affect the skin 
(pigmentation, acne, dullness) and how fast it responds to treatment. When you connect her skin concern to 
what’s happening inside her body, with empathy, two things happen: she feels truly understood, and she finally 
understands why internal care (diet, consistency, patience) is not optional. This is care first — the trust it builds is 
everything.
Stay in your lane — important
You connect and care. The doctor diagnoses and decides. Never diagnose a condition, name 
medicines, or give medical advice. You gently acknowledge what she has already shared (or what the 
doctor has noted), link it to her skin in simple, caring language, and reinforce the internal-care plan. 
Anything clinical — the doctor leads, and you both speak in one voice.
Know your basics — so you sound informed
This is awareness, not diagnosis. Knowing the basics lets you speak with confidence and empathy — she should feel ‘this counsellor 
understands my body, not just my face.’ You inform; the doctor diagnoses.
Thyroid — in simple words
What it is: the thyroid is a small gland in the neck that controls the body’s energy and metabolism (how fast the 
body works). When it makes too little hormone it’s hypothyroid (slow); too much is hyperthyroid (fast). 
Hypothyroid is the more common one in women.
Why it happens: often genetic / runs in families, autoimmune (the body’s own system affecting the gland), iodine 
imbalance, stress, post-pregnancy changes, or simply hormonal shifts women go through. It is very common — 
not something to be ashamed of.
Common symptoms: tiredness / low energy, weight changes, hair fall or thinning, feeling cold, mood changes, 
irregular periods — and for skin: dryness, dullness, puffiness, and slow healing.
The skin link: because thyroid slows the body’s repair and circulation, skin can become dry, dull and slower to 
respond — so treatment results may take a little longer, which is completely manageable when we know about it.
PCOS / Hormonal imbalance — in simple words
What it is: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) is a common hormonal condition in women where hormones — 
especially androgens — go a little out of balance, often with irregular periods.
Why it happens: genetics, insulin resistance, lifestyle and diet, stress and weight changes all play a role. Again — 
very common, and very manageable.
Common symptoms: irregular periods, weight gain, excess facial/body hair, hair thinning on the scalp — and for 
skin: acne, oiliness, and pigmentation (especially around the jaw, neck and cheeks).
The skin link: the hormonal shifts trigger more oil and pigment, so acne and pigmentation can be stubborn — 
which is exactly why internal care (diet, consistency) alongside treatment matters so much.
How to use this: weave a line or two naturally into the conversation so she feels you understand — never lecture, 
never diagnose. “Thyroid energy aur metabolism ko slow karta hai, isiliye skin thodi dry aur slow heal hoti hai” is 
enough to show knowledge. For anything specific to her case, the doctor leads.
How to speak — the empathy bridge

blocks.title: Page 2
blocks.text:
Three steps, every time: 1) Acknowledge her condition warmly and without alarm. 2) Link it to her skin so the 
‘why’ finally makes sense. 3) Reassure + redirect to what you can control together — treatment + diet + 
consistency. Calm, warm, never scary.
PCOS / Hormonal Imbalance
“Maam aap ne bataya tha aap ko PCOS / hormonal imbalance hai — main samajhti hoon, aur achha 
hua aap ne share kiya. Yeh bahut common hai, aur is mein ghabrane wali koi baat nahi.
Hota yeh hai ki jab hormones thode imbalance hote hain, toh uska seedha asar skin pe aata hai — 
pigmentation, acne, ya dullness. Isiliye kabhi kabhi skin treatment ke baad bhi thoda time leti hai, 
kyunki hum andar aur bahar dono pe kaam kar rahe hain.
Achhi baat yeh hai — hum dono pe saath kaam karenge: treatment bahar se, aur diet aur consistency 
andar se. Yahi reason hai humari dietician aap ke saath rahegi. Aap akeli nahi ho is mein.”
Coaching: “Achha hua aap ne share kiya” makes her feel safe, not judged. The link (hormones → skin → slower 
response) turns her frustration into understanding. Then redirect to the controllables — and bring in the dietitian 
as care, not upsell.
Thyroid
“Maam aap ka thyroid hai — thank you for telling me, yeh jaanna humare liye important hai. Thyroid 
body ki energy aur balance ko affect karta hai, aur skin bhi usse juda hua hai — dryness, dullness, ya 
slow healing aa sakti hai.
Isiliye aap ki journey mein hum thoda extra dhyaan rakhenge — treatment ke saath aap ki internal 
health ko bhi support karenge. Aap apni thyroid medication aur reports doctor maam ke saath zaroor 
share karna, taaki hum aap ke liye best plan bana sakein.
Aap tension mat lena — hum is ko dhyaan mein rakhte hue aap ko results denge.”
Coaching: Keep it reassuring, never clinical. The one concrete ask — share medication + reports with the doctor 
— keeps the medical lead where it belongs while you hold the care.
When she hasn’t named a condition but skin is slow
“Maam kabhi kabhi skin andar ki cheezon ko reflect karti hai — hormones, nutrition, neend, stress. 
Agar aap ko koi cheez pata ho jaise PCOS, thyroid, ya cycle irregular ho, toh please share kar dena — 
isse hum aap ka plan aur behtar bana sakte hain. Yeh poori tarah private rahega.”
Coaching: This gently opens the door for her to disclose, framed as ‘so we can help you better,’ with a privacy 
reassurance. Whatever she shares, route the medical side to the doctor.
Remember
Empathy first, link second, redirect third. You make her feel understood and explain the ‘why’ — the doctor 
handles the medical. A client who understands why her skin behaves the way it does becomes patient, 
consistent, and loyal. That understanding is the kindest, most powerful thing you can give her.
